QtyComponent / specification

Arduino is the tool.
ESP32 is the board.

  1. Install Arduino IDE and Espressif’s Arduino-ESP32 board package ↗.
  2. Select ESP32S3 Dev Module. Match flash/PSRAM settings to your exact N8R8 board. Enable USB CDC On Boot if using native USB.
  3. Disconnect the external 5 V feed and high-current peripherals before connecting the PC’s USB cable.
  4. Upload this bring-up sketch. Open Serial Monitor at 115200 and compare detected addresses with the wiring map.
  5. Install the libraries below and test each module separately, then implement your application logic.

Application libraries

    This download is a pin-configured I²C / digital-input diagnostic. It does not implement the finished clock, timer, sensor drivers, RGB protocol, or voice pipeline. It has not been compiled or tested on hardware here.

    01 / PROVE IT

    Breadboard + modules

    Start with the development board and breakouts. Verify rails, scan I²C, test inputs, then add LED and audio loads. Route high-current power with rated leads and terminals.

    02 / MAKE IT SOLID

    Socketed carrier

    Transfer the tested connections to perfboard or a custom carrier with headers. Keep the antenna clear, sensors ventilated, and USB accessible. Measure your actual modules and mounting holes.

    03 / ENGINEER IT

    Design a real PCB

    In KiCad, draw the full schematic, select verified footprints, place components, route power and signals, and run ERC/DRC. Review current capacity, grounding, decoupling, and enclosure fit before fabrication.

    Placement rules for this application

      The website is a modular assembly and connection guide. Its 3D board and lines are not dimensioned CAD, routed copper, an electrical simulation, or manufacturing files. No Gerbers are supplied. The proposed wiring is not physically validated.

      POWER PLAN

      One power source at a time. Use a regulated, current-limited 5 V / 2 A source for standalone assembly. Disconnect USB when feeding the 5V header. Disconnect the external 5 V lead before USB programming. All GPIO signals stay at 3.3 V; the LED buffer is the explicit exception on its output side.
